proofUses.reason: A direct column-mass estimate treats both terms of B2; no pointwise kernel-reversal identity is assumed.

An explicit alternating route distributes the cosine weight. Both end sums, the parity-dependent connectors, and the two central terms are calculated; the first central term is bounded by T squared times W through two summable factors.
Removing both trivial triangles leaves the W(0;k) term. The nontrivial triangle mass is at most three halves T; explicit estimates give 31/2 times T Delta W, hence the stated constant 16.

Polynomially weighted geometric summation gives summable coefficient frequency bounds and then absolute second moments. Bounds on W and H, and any needed quantitative smallness, remain explicit premises.
